findings.highlight: And he’s also the student council president, so you’d think he’d take to it like a duck to water, but…
findings.evidenceJa: しかも生徒会長だっていうんだから、まさに鬼に金棒、虎に翼といったところなのだが
findings.governingReading: Issei already has elegant looks and immense popularity; adding the student-council presidency is strength piled upon strength, like an iron club for an ogre or wings for a tiger.
findings.explanation: Take to it like a duck to water describes natural aptitude for the presidency, replacing the source's accumulation of social advantages and breaking the contrast with his deliberately plain habits.

findings.highlight: “Hm. Hot tea is certainly a good way to start a morning.” He’s just sipping tea like this, so he’s not that firm.
findings.evidenceJa: 「うむ、やはり朝は舌がしびれる程の熱湯がよい」なんて言いながら番茶をすすっているもんだから、いまいち締まらない。
findings.governingReading: Issei solemnly insists that mornings call for water hot enough to numb the tongue, yet he is sipping humble bancha; the combination keeps his impressive profile from quite coming together.
findings.explanation: Generic hot tea removes the excessive heat and humble tea type, while not that firm misreads 締まらない as a personal lack of firmness rather than the comic failure of the image to look dignified or cool.

findings.highlight: can you hand me the torque screwdriver? The biggest one.
findings.evidenceJa: マイナスドライバーくれ。一番おっきいヤツな。
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks for the largest flathead screwdriver, using the standard Japanese term マイナスドライバー.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a torque screwdriver, a different tool category, inside a scene whose purpose is to establish the exactness of Shirou's repair work.

findings.highlight: I would have had to “strengthen” it in a very unamatuerish way.
findings.evidenceJa: その時は素人じゃない方法で“強化”しなくてはいけなかった
findings.governingReading: If the heating tube itself had failed, Shirou would have needed to use the non-amateur method of magical Strengthening.
findings.explanation: Unamatuerish is misspelled and forms an ungainly invented adjective in a key transition from ordinary repair to magecraft.

findings.highlight: That is the “magic” Emiya Shirou learned from Kiritsugu.
findings.evidenceJa: それが切嗣に教わった、衛宮士郎の“魔術”である。
findings.governingReading: The structural diagnosis and possible Strengthening are identified as Shirou's 魔術, the learnable technical practice distinguished elsewhere from 魔法.
findings.explanation: Magic collapses the source's marked magecraft category into the separate term used for Magic, repeating an already documented system-level terminology failure.

findings.highlight: They say that the battle of the magus comes in reading the center, the core of things instantaneously, and changing it faster than anything else.
findings.evidenceJa: 物事の核である中心を即座に読みとり、誰よりも速く変化させるのが魔術師たちの戦いだと言う。
findings.governingReading: A magus's contest is to read the central core of a thing instantly and alter it faster than anyone else can.
findings.explanation: The battle of the magus comes in is malformed, and anything else changes the comparison from rival practitioners to all other things, obscuring the competitive mechanism being explained.

findings.highlight: It’s commonly believed that only teachers and guys like Issei can even talk to her.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂と話が出来るのは一成と先生たちぐらいなもの、というのが男どもの通説だ。
findings.governingReading: The boys' received wisdom is that essentially only Issei and the teachers can speak with Rin.
findings.explanation: Guys like Issei turns one specifically named peer into an open class of similar boys, weakening the extremity of Rin's perceived social distance and Issei's exceptional position.

findings.highlight: We barely made it. Thank you, Emiya. I caused you trouble again. I would be a failure as a friend if I made you late doing things for me.
findings.evidenceJa: ギリギリ間にあったか。すまんな衛宮、また苦労をかけた。頼み事をした上に遅刻させては友人失格だ
findings.governingReading: Having barely returned in time, Issei apologizes to Emiya for causing him trouble again and says making a friend late after asking a favor would disqualify him as a friend.
findings.explanation: Thank you reverses the explicit apology すまんな into gratitude, even as the following sentences continue the apologetic reasoning.

findings.highlight: I was wondering what you’d been doing since quitting the club, but all you’ve been doing is helping out Ryuudou? It’s not my concern, but don’t do anything to bring the club into disrepute, okay? You’re pretty uncommitted after all.
findings.evidenceJa: 部活を辞めてから何をしてるかと思えば柳洞の太鼓持ち？　僕には関係ないけどさ、うちの評判を落とすような事はしないでよね。君、なんていうか節操ないからさ
findings.governingReading: Shinji sneers that after quitting the club Shirou has become Ryuudou's sycophant or flatterer, then calls him lacking in principles or restraint.
findings.explanation: Helping out removes the insult from 太鼓持ち, while uncommitted recasts moral opportunism or indiscriminate conduct as failure to commit, making Shinji's attack both milder and differently directed.

findings.highlight: “…What? I don’t want to. I’m scared she’ll bite me if I go near her…” “…She’s not a Mimic or anything. She won’t go that far.”
findings.evidenceJa: 「……えー、やだよー……近づいた途端、パクッって食べられたら怖いもん……」「……ミミックじゃあるまいし、さすがに藤村でもそこまでやらねえだろ」
findings.governingReading: The student fears being suddenly eaten with a chomp upon approaching, prompting the explicit comparison to a Mimic, a monster that devours someone who comes close.
findings.explanation: Bite me reduces being eaten to a bite, so the Mimic reply no longer answers the specific imagined mechanism that set up the joke.

findings.highlight: The day she’s in charge of us, we’d get into the regionals!
findings.evidenceJa: タイガーが顧問になった日にゃ、オレたち甲子園いっちまうぞ！？
findings.governingReading: The student jokes that if Taiga became the baseball club adviser, they would reach Koshien, the nationally emblematic high-school baseball destination.
findings.explanation: Regionals replaces the named culmination with an earlier generic competition level, materially lowering the hyperbolic promise and deleting the proper cultural reference.

findings.highlight: please address your teacher as ‘Fujimura-sensei’. I’ll get mad if you call me that again.
findings.evidenceJa: 先生のことは藤村先生って言わなくちゃダメなんだから。次に名前で呼んだら怒るからね？
findings.governingReading: Taiga tells Gotou to address her as Fujimura-sensei and warns that she will get angry if he calls her by her given name again.
findings.explanation: That grammatically points back to Fujimura-sensei, so the English warns him against using the very address it has just required and reverses the rule.

findings.highlight: We’re starting class. Day monitor, the bows.
findings.evidenceJa: 授業を始める。日直、礼を
findings.governingReading: The arriving teacher announces the start of class and directs the student on duty to lead the formal bow or greeting.
findings.explanation: The bows is an unexplained plural noun rather than a command to bow, leaving the routine classroom instruction grammatically and pragmatically malformed.

findings.highlight: They’re restocking inventory at work, and they asked me to come if I can as any help is appreciated.
findings.evidenceJa: 飲み屋の棚卸しで、とにかく男手は多いほどいいから手伝いに来られるのなら来てほしい、という物だった。
findings.governingReading: The bar is taking inventory and has asked Shirou to come if he can because the more male hands available for the job, the better.
findings.explanation: Restocking changes counting or checking stock into replenishing it, while any help is appreciated deletes the stated desire for additional male labor.

findings.evidenceJa: よし続けろ！　ガコロウトンの計じゃ！
findings.governingReading: Keep it up! It is the Gakorouton stratagem!
findings.explanation: The English removes the named comic stratagem entirely and substitutes a generic description of punishment; the omission is certain even though the allusion’s provenance remains unresolved.
